2026-09-22: never let a transcription pipeline delete its own evidence. dictation.sh removed /tmp/xhisper.wav after every run, so three rounds of debugging were blind. Patch: copy to /tmp/xhisper-last.wav before each rm. Then the FIRST captured real attempt settled the question in one measurement (spectral centroid 24Hz). Also: when an acoustic loopback with TTS returns no_speech>0.9 for BOTH mics, the TTS never reached them (speech-dispatcher routes to its own device) - that is an inconclusive test, not a negative result; do not read it as 'the mic is fine'.

2026-09-22: route 'BT headset mic is silent/garbage' intents to a spectral check FIRST (band energy + centroid + flatness on a saved capture). Band-energy split (<300 / 300-3400 / >3400 Hz) separates a dead/rumble mic from a healthy one in one command, before touching kernels, codecs, or profile logic. A hardware mic fault can survive every software fix; the pragmatic resolution is to route dictation to the laptop mic (PREFER_BT_MIC=0 default) and confirm the headset on another host.

2026-09-22 ROOT CAUSE (dictation hallucinated 'Thank you.'): pw-record from PipeWire 1.0.5 produces corrupted capture on this host. A/B on the SAME source: pw-record -> low-freq hash that Whisper maps to 'Thank you.'; parec (pacat 16.1) and ffmpeg -f pulse -> verbatim correct transcription. xhisper recorded with pw-record, so EVERY dictation attempt was destroyed at capture, regardless of microphone. Fix: xhisper now records with 'parec --rate=16000 --channels=1 --file-format=wav'; dictation.sh active-recording probe updated to match. Validated: JFK fixture through the patched path transcribes verbatim. NOTE: all earlier mic diagnoses (incl. 'the BT headset mic is broken') were measured with pw-record and are therefore INVALID.

2026-09-22 RETRACTION of the earlier pw-record claim (same day). That was a FALSE ALARM caused by an apples-to-oranges A/B: 'pw-record --target NAME' silently falls back to the DEFAULT source, while 'parec --device=NAME' honors its flag. When both tools were pointed at the SAME source (monitor set as default, no target flags), BOTH captured JFK verbatim (parec centroid 893Hz, pw-record 885Hz, both 96.9% in the speech band). LESSON: before declaring a capture tool corrupt, force every tool onto the identical source via the DEFAULT rather than per-tool target flags, and verify the tools agree. A '--target/--device' flag that is silently ignored produces two identical-looking captures and one bogus bug report.

2026-09-22 dictation investigation, verified facts: (1) Groq whisper-large-v3 transcribes a known good file (OpenAI JFK fixture) verbatim, so the API leg is fine. (2) pw-record, parec and ffmpeg all capture correctly. (3) NO microphone on this host captured any acoustic signal in testing - internal mic at Internal Mic Boost=0 gives peak 10 of 32767 (essentially zero), at boost=3 gives a flat -35dBFS noise floor with no syllable dynamics (peak 2395), and the BT headset mic gives ~95% energy below 300Hz. (4) UNRESOLVED: the only acoustic source available was the laptop speakers and they could not be confirmed audible, so 'both mics are deaf' could not be separated from 'the speakers are silent'. Next diagnostic must use a HUMAN-VERIFIED acoustic source. Beware: the internal mic has Capture=+30dB AND Internal Mic Boost=+30dB cascaded.

2026-09-22 TRUE ROOT CAUSE of the dictation failures (after 3 wrong calls): the RECORDER, not the mic, not the API, not pw-record, not the gates. Measuring 4s of wall clock: pacat/parec wrote 2.00s of samples in 6 of 8 runs (2x-speed, unintelligible -> Whisper always answered 'Thank you.'); pw-record through the default source behaved the same; ffmpeg wrote 4.04s every time. xhisper (pw-record) and vox-v1 (parec) both destroyed every capture BEFORE transcription. Fix: record with ffmpeg -f pulse -i <explicit device> -ar 16000 -ac 1. LESSON: a rate bug yields a capture that is LOUD, envelope speech-shaped, and passes every level/band gate, yet unintelligible. THE CHECK THAT CATCHES IT: compare file duration against wall-clock recording time - 2x speed instantly shows as half the expected duration. Add it to any capture pipeline.

2026-09-22: every microphone verdict issued earlier this session (internal mic dead / BT headset mic defective / stalled SCO buffer) was measured with parec or pw-record, i.e. with a recorder writing rate-corrupted audio. Those verdicts are UNRELIABLE and must be re-derived with ffmpeg. The user's headset also works on their phone, independently contradicting the 'headset broken' call. Rule: never characterise a microphone with a recorder you have not first validated against wall-clock duration.

Voice-activity gating: level, band-energy delta, spectral flatness and frame-RMS spread EACH produce false positives alone. Level rated a stalled -3.7dBFS capture as loud; band-delta rated -39dBFS room noise as SPEECH (delta 5.8 < 12); spread rated a slow infrasonic drift as syllables. Only all four together separate speech/noise/stalled. Calibrated: speech flat<0.05 spread>25 delta~0.4 | room noise flat>0.32 spread<11 | stalled flat<0.01 delta>16.

Bluetooth audio on this QCA9377 host: SBC-XQ (a2dp-sink-sbc_xq) silently kills the A2DP transport ('Failure in Bluetooth audio transport' in wireplumber) AND corrupts the HFP uplink - the headset mic then yields pure sub-300Hz drift that fakes 'stalled capture'. Switching the card to plain SBC (a2dp-sink profile) fixed BOTH playback and the mic in one change. Diagnose BT by watching wireplumber's transport errors, not by measuring the mic. Also: the internal mic on this Acer is a DMIC ('Conn = Digital' on pin 0x12) and transduces nothing at all - a loud 1kHz beep at 120% volume moved its capture by 0.0 dB.
